newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds gave up intraday gains to end another quiet day little changed from their previous closing levels.
At 1421 GMT the benchmark R150 stock was at 15.365 percent from 15.37 percent late on Tuesday after moving to the day's worst levels in late trade.
Dealers said early bonds started strong as players were caught slightly short of stock late on Tuesday but shaved gains on the back of rand vulnerability and late profit-taking by jobbers.
The market was described as lacking in direction and big institutions were conspicuous by their absence.
"There's no direction...institutions are not involved save for a bit of pushing and pulling and without the big institutions we can't channel the market into any clear direction," a trader noted.
Dealers were divided over future direction.

Some optimistically predicted a break of 15.24 percent on the downside as the next target based on fairly sound fundamentals while others were more cautious, favouring a sideways move in a 15.30 to 15.40 percent band.
In the absence of fresh economic or political news, the market would take its cue from the rand in the next couple of days, they said.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 13.96 million rand of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling a net 160.44 million rand of bonds on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 6.35 billion rand on Tuesday from 4.66 billion rand on Monday.
The rand broke its sleepy pattern seen over the last few days to weaken to a worst 4.5380 bid during the afternoon session.
At 1429 GMT the currency was at 4.5375/5425 on the dollar from 4.5315/5365 overnight.
"The market was caught short of dollars and players trimmed down position in afternoon trade," a senior trader said.
"It's looking a bit weaker but one must remember that it's still holding in the 4.51/52 to 4.54/55 range with good two-way trade. Nothing substantial is really happening," the dealer added.
Traders agreed it was difficult to predict whether the currency would break at the top or bottom side.
"It all depends on what kind of an order hits the market," one said.
Against the crosses the rand was last trading at 7.0977/1078 from 7.0830/0954 on Tuesday and was at 0.3364/3369 marks from 0.3364/3369 marks previously.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.75 and 15.95 percent, while 90-day BAs were also unchanged at between 15.20 and 15.40 percent.
The daily shortage was quoted at 7.823 billion rand on Tuesday from 8.405 billion rand on Monday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
